item.title: Vila Marebo / Frederico Zanelato | Arquitetos
item.dc:creator: Susanna Moreira
item.description: The design of Vila Marebo, in southern Bahia, was born from the invitation of a long-time partner. The premise was clear: to create two independent blocks connected by a footbridge and a generous pergola. More than a residence, the proposal was to conceive a true village that embraces the lot. This fluid zoning encourages encounters, conversations, and leisure, transforming the pathways and surrounding spaces into environments of pure warmth and sensory experience.

item.title: casa POP / gon architects
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: Casa POP is based on the premise that there is no such thing as a standard user, and therefore architecture must adapt to unique ways of living. The original home, a 78 m² apartment located in Vicálvaro, was built in the 2000s under the rigid standards of the traditional nuclear family, resulting in a highly compartmentalized layout full of hallways. This distribution was obsolete for its owners, Santiago and Ángel, a couple whose lives revolve around enjoyment, knowledge, and culture.

item.title: Imbriani – Renovation of Two Apartments in Milan / co.arch studio
item.dc:creator: Cristina Popescu
item.description: The project transforms two small early 20th-century apartments in Milan's Bovisa district, organized around a shared threshold. This threshold became the conceptual starting point of the intervention: a spatial device that separates and connects two distinct domestic identities, expressed immediately through two contrasting chromatic atmospheres—terra red and matcha green.

item.title: Between Burning Forests and Utopian Cities: Designing the Climate Transition
item.dc:creator: Olivia Poston
item.description: There is no shortage of ways to imagine what the world will look like after a climate catastrophe. Genres of movies and novels have been built around the question of what happens when contemporary safeguards fail, from dystopian fiction and post-apocalyptic literature to disaster films, graphic novels, and video games. Burning forests, submerged cities, abandoned infrastructure, resource scarcity, and mass displacement are a familiar visual and narrative vocabulary. We have become remarkably fluent in imagining the consequences of a world that fails to respond to climate change.

item.title: Cabins at the Tip, Sunny Lakes, Senec / ER Atelier
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: The project of two recreational buildings at the tip of Sunny Lakes in Senec approaches two separate structures as a single architectural and landscape composition. Located on a prominent waterfront peninsula, the site is characterized by an unregulated mixture of recreational buildings from different periods and architectural styles. Rather than introducing another isolated expression, the proposal seeks to redefine the entire tip through a unified architectural language, while preserving the memory of the site and strengthening its relationship with the lake and the public realm.

item.title: The Full Moon / SHISUO design office
item.dc:creator: 韩爽 - HAN Shuang
item.description: Invited by the Power Station of Art (PSA), SHISUO Design Office has unveiled "The Full Moon" an urban public art installation celebrating the Mid-Autumn Festival in Shanghai. The installation was realized in collaboration with Shi Qinling, a Shanghai-style paper-cutting inheritor, and is themed around the moon, rabbits, and the art of paper-cutting. Across various cultures, the rabbit holds a unique place in the human imagination as one of the few animal figures beloved by all. In China's classical Mid-Autumn folklore, the rabbit is a constant companion to the moon—the moon symbolizes the cyclical waxing and waning of existence, while the rabbit metaphorically represents the vitality, growth, and flourishing of all beings.

item.title: PH Olaguer / CDC ARQ
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: Rather than adding elements, the project proposes concentrating functions to free up space. Spatial continuity, the connection to the courtyard, and a single, continuous piece of millwork that guides the journey create a small yet spatially generous home, where architecture serves as a tool for spatial organization.

item.title: Residência em Campos do Jordão / Gil Mello Arquitetura
item.dc:creator: Susanna Moreira
item.description: The presented project is the result of a complete renovation, based on the premise of reusing the existing perimeter walls, foundations and slabs. This design strategy aimed to optimize resources and execution time, made possible by a feasibility study that confirmed the capacity of the existing structure to accommodate the new program of needs.

item.title: Villas Raices / Vince Studio
item.dc:creator: Valentina Díaz
item.description: Villas Raíces was born from the intention of inhabiting the mountain with the least possible impact, allowing the architecture to adapt to the terrain and not the other way around.

item.title: Jeronimo Faria Lima Building / Perkins&Will São Paulo
item.dc:creator: Nana Dokua
item.description: At one of São Paulo’s most emblematic corners—where the intensity of Brigadeiro Faria Lima Avenue meets the walkable scale of Jeronimo da Veiga Street—Jeronimo Faria Lima does not seek to assert itself through height, form, or presence in the skyline alone. The project is guided by a deeper ambition: to make the encounter between architecture and the city a fundamental part of the experience.

item.title: Panorama House / Studio B Architecture + Interiors
item.dc:creator: Hana Abdel
item.description: The Panorama House project involved both renovating and expanding an existing residence originally designed by the renowned mid-century architect, James Hunter. The structure's distinguished heritage and the innovative architectural solution garnered it recognition as a Historic Landmark during the rigorous approval process. Designed for homeowners seeking a peaceful retreat, the residence carefully balances privacy amidst cherished landmarks and bustling trails while embracing the natural beauty of its surroundings.

item.title: Corte Renèe Resort / Bricolo Falsarella
item.dc:creator: Nina Vuga
item.description: Nestled among the green hills of Lake Garda, an 1800s farmhouse was reborn through a restoration project that created a small hospitality structure respecting the local culture and traditions: Corte Renèe.

item.title: TC 175- Moneo Brock
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
This issue traces almost two decades of work by the international firm Moneo Brock, founded in New York in 1993 by Belén Moneo and Jeff Brock, and based in Madrid since 2002. Across 320 pages, the publication presents a selection of works built between 2007 and 2026, ranging from urban infrastructures and educational facilities to leisure spaces, domestic architecture, and object design, with projects realized in Spain, Mexico, Colombia, and the Dominican Republic.

Three critical essays frame the reading of the work. Stan Allen examines the studio's commitment to public space and the collective dimension of architecture, highlighting how each building

item.title: 2027 Beam Camp Project Open Call
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Beam Center seeks design proposals for an ambitious public artwork that will be brought to life through collaborations between youth, Beam Camp staff and the selected proposer. Projects will be realized by a community of more than 100 young people at Beam Camp in July 2026.

Beam Camp is a specialized summer camp for building and collaboration located in Strafford, NH. Our award-winning program offers youth (ages 9-17) the opportunity to cultivate hands-on skills while exploring innovative thinking, design, problem solving and the creative process.

Every year, Beam Camp solicits proposals for unique and spectacular large-scale projects that serve as the centerpiece

item.title: Space Architecture Week
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
During World Space Week, architecture expands its boundaries. The new space race raises a fundamental question for today's designers: how do we imagine, build, and inhabit beyond Earth?

From October 5 to 8, 2026, the Faculty of Architecture, Design and Urbanism at the University of Buenos Aires will host Space Architecture Week, a Latin American gathering that will bring together architecture, science, technology, and design.

Through workshops, a space architecture hackathon, international guests, talks, interviews, and exhibitions, students, professionals, and specialists will explore new ways to inhabit the Moon, Mars, and other environments.

item.title: Launch of the Glossary for the City of Our Future
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Glossary for the City of Our Future Gathers Experts to Reflect on the Cities of Tomorrow with Hope

What kind of city do we want to build for future generations? This is the central question of Glossary for the City of Our Future with Hope, a book organized and edited by architect and professor Thereza Christina Couto Carvalho. The launch will take place on September 28 at 6:30 PM at Livraria da Travessa in Ipanema, Rio de Janeiro.

Published by Rio Books, the book brings together 47 contributors—including researchers, architects, urban planners, and experts from various fields—to offer an interdisciplinary reflection on contemporary challenges.

item.title: Continental Drift: Encounters, North and South
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Continental Drift: Encounters, North and South
An exhibition presented by browngrotta arts
October 17–25, 2026 | Wilton, Connecticut

This October, browngrotta arts presents Continental Drift: Encounters, North and South, an exhibition exploring how artistic tradition migrates, transforms, and takes root across the Americas — and beyond. The show brings together more than 40 leading fiber and sculptural artists, tracing lines of influence that cross borders, generations, and continents.

About the Exhibition

The exhibition takes its name from the geological process by which continents slowly separate, collide, and reshape one another over time — a metaphor the gallery uses to examine how artistic traditions move across

item.title: CFP: Porto, Portugal – Heritages 2027: UNESCO Perspectives
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
This University of Porto conference marks the 55th anniversary of the UNESCO World Heritage Convention. It explores heritage across art, architecture, history, museums, digital culture, tourism, sustainability and communities, making it fully interdisciplinary.

Taking place in Porto, it is held in a city that characterizes the issues at play: a coastal city, a historic maritime centre and Europe’s first protected wine region. Its core is a World Heritage Site and a National Monument of Portugal.

From this unique setting, the conference considers questions of heritage globally.

Publications by UCL Press & Intellect Books.

Conference Type:
In-person & Virtual (Pre-recorded and written

item.title: Tallinn Design Festival 2026: Future of Product Design
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Tallinn Design Festival / Disainiöö returns from 28 September to 4 October 2026 for its 21st edition, bringing together contemporary Estonian design, international designers, exhibitions, talks, installations, workshops and city-wide events.

Taking place primarily at Põhjala Factory, a former industrial complex in northern Tallinn, this year’s festival focuses on the theme “Future of Product Design”.

The programme asks a fundamental question: in a world already filled with products, what should designers create next?

Across exhibitions and discussions, the festival explores how circular economy principles, new technologies, artificial intelligence, material innovation, longevity and changing consumption habits are influencing both the objects we create and

item.title: The Lives of Ephemeral Form
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
The Lives of Ephemeral Form examines how architecture persists, changes, and disappears through its records, and what happens when those records are themselves unstable.

Developed as part of the Architectural Institute of Japan’s 140th anniversary program, the exhibition is the first phase of a two-year project devoted to the act of documentation. It brings together installations, archival research, photography, moving images, screenings, talks, guided programs, and work carried out publicly in the gallery.

Architecture is often associated with permanence. Yet buildings depend on unstable conditions: economic circumstances, technologies, changing patterns of use, material resources, and the less visible forces that transform cities.

item.title: INC 20th Anniversary & Monograph Book Launch
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
Please join us to celebrate INC's 20th anniversary and the release of our first monograph, Us Is More.

​The evening will be held at one of our newest projects, Manifest 002 at Union Market in Washington, DC.

​Moderated by award-winning, DC-based multidisciplinary artist and former Global Head of Purpose for Eaton Hotels, Sheldon Scott, the conversation will bring together INC Founding Partner Adam Rolston, Manifest CEO and visionary KJ Hughes, and writer, curator, historian, and Us Is More contributor Camille Okhio to discuss the design, collaborations, and ideas that shaped the book.

​Refreshments and copies of the monograph will be

item.title: interihotel
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
interihotel is the meeting point for hospitality design. A leading event where interior design, architecture, products, technology and business come together to explore the future of hotels, restaurants and hospitality spaces.

Discover the latest trends in furniture, lighting, materials, textiles and contract solutions, explore innovative projects and concepts, and connect with architects, interior designers, brands, manufacturers, hoteliers and other professionals from across the industry.

The scale of the event reflects the strength of the sector: the latest edition, interihotel BCN25, brought together 11,675 professionals from 53 countries and 291 exhibiting brands, while identifying more than 2,500 active hospitality projects.

More than a trade

item.title: Into the Frame - Workshop with Kees Christiaanse
item.dc:creator: Rene Submissions
item.description:
FROM FRAGMENTS TO AN URBAN FRAMEWORK

YARD is pleased to announce INTO THE FRAME, an intensive urban design workshop in Yerevan led by architect and urbanist Kees Christiaanse.

The workshop explores how fragmented urban territories can be connected, transformed, and reimagined as part of a larger urban framework.

THE WORKSHOP

25-30 participants will work in small groups across a selected fragment of Yerevan, continuously relating their ideas to a shared physical model at 1:1000 or 1:500 scale.

Following Kees Christiaanse’s “simultaneous chess” method, participants will work across multiple scales, developing analysis and spatial propositions in parallel within Yerevan’s complex urban fabric of

item.title: Light Through the Wall: Indian House Interiors Shaped by Brick Jali
item.dc:creator: Miwa Negoro
item.description: A brick façade does more than define the façade of a house. When designed as a porous screen, it becomes an intermediary between inside and outside, shaping the atmosphere and environmental conditions of the spaces behind it. Across contemporary Indian residential architecture, brick jali — a perforated or lattice brick screen — has been reinterpreted with a contemporary sensibility, drawing on vernacular architectural elements.
